prior_passes.sheet_conflicts: Sheet length is 38.0 km. The only literal, well-documented, geocodable place named 'Badr El Din' (the BAPETCO flagship BED oil/gas complex near Abu Gharadig, Matrouh governorate) is ~159 km great-circle distance from the derived Faramid/East Obayed start point -- a 4x mismatch that cannot be a 38 km pipeline. This means 'Badr El Din Company' in the sourcing (Egypt Oil & Gas: 'extending another line from the Faramid field to Badr El Din Company to process 24 mcf/d') most plausibly refers to BAPETCO the corporate operator (whose name derives from its Badr El Din field), not the distant Badr El Din facility itself. BAPETCO's own concession list separately includes Badr el Din, North East Abu Gharadig, Obaiyed, Sitra, and Matruh as distinct concessions, and a 'BAPETCO Obaiyed Gas Plant' facility in Marsa Matrouh Governorate was referenced (bizmideast.com) -- geographically consistent with a 38 km tie-in from Faramid -- but that page returned HTTP 403 on url_verifier and direct fetch, so its content/coordinates could not be independently confirmed and it is NOT included as a cited source.
prior_passes.notes: Start point corroborated by 3+ independent outlets (Rigzone, NSEnergy, World Oil, plus a Zacks search snippet) describing the Faramid South discovery as sitting in the East Obayed concession, ~30 km NW of the Meleiha concession -- consistent with the prior_suggestion. Coordinate is a computed offset from the geocoded village of Meleiha (OSM), so concession-scale, not wellhead-precise. End point: the pipeline-connection claim itself (Faramid -> 'Badr El Din Company', 24 mcf/d, matching the sheet's implied ~24-25 MMcf/d) is directly and independently sourced (Egypt Oil & Gas, citing Agiba Petroleum/EGAS investment plans) so the NAME is solid, but the corresponding PHYSICAL location is ambiguous -- the only citable, geocodable 'Badr El Din' place is BAPETCO's namesake field/complex near Abu Gharadig, which is geographically incompatible (159 km) with a 38 km pipeline from Faramid. The likelier physical destination is a nearer BAPETCO-operated facility in the Obaiyed/Matrouh concession cluster (same company, same corporate branding), but no verifiable, url_verifier-passing public source could pin down that facility's precise location within the research budget available. Set resolved:false and flagged for a follow-up pass focused specifically on locating BAPETCO's Obaiyed-area gas plant/tie-in point (try BAPETCO/Shell Egypt annual reports, EGAS concession maps, or imagery around the Meleiha/East Obayed cluster for a labeled gas facility) before drawing a two-point route -- a route to the distant Abu Gharadig Badr El Din point would misrepresent the pipeline's actual geometry by roughly 4x.

RETRY confirmed Obaiyed is a real, large, distinct BAPETCO/Capricorn Energy/Cheiron Petroleum-operated Jurassic gas/condensate field (described as Egypt's largest onshore gas field) in the same general Western Desert region as Faramid -- supporting the theory that the true tie-in point is somewhere in the Obaiyed cluster, not Abu Gharadig -- but no source gives an actual coordinate, address, or specific named sub-facility for a BAPETCO/Obaiyed gas plant (checked BAPETCO/Capricorn Energy materials, OSM/Nominatim, industry press). One paywalled academic abstract (tandfonline, HTTP 403, not citable) placed the Obaiyed field between latitudes 31 02'-31 12'N with no longitude -- too imprecise and not independently verifiable to use. A Scribd document titled 'Obaiyed Area Gas Wells Road Map' (wells OB01-OB37 with export-pipeline flow lines) exists but its map/coordinates could not be extracted via fetch; flagged for a human to open directly in a future pass. The prior bizmideast.com 'BAPETCO Obaiyed Gas Plant' lead remains HTTP 403-blocked and unusable.

Set resolved:false; recommend a follow-up with a fresh search budget to open the Scribd 'Obaiyed Area Gas Wells Road Map' PDF directly, or pull BAPETCO/Cheiron/EGAS concession-map PDFs, to pin down the true endpoint.
